title: Thy Servants in the Temple Watched
description: Thy Servants in the Temple Watched in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 589, “The Day-Spring From on High”, where the book credits them to Sp. of Psalms.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy ser-vants in the tem-ple watched The daw-ning of the day, Im-pa-tient with its ear-liest beams Their ho-ly vows to pay; And cho-sen saints far off be-held That great and glo-rious morn, When the glad day spring from on high Aus-pi-cious-ly should dawn.

lines: Thy servants in the temple watched
And chosen saints far off beheld
When the glad day-spring from on high
On us the Sun of Righteousness
With grateful hearts and holy zeal,
And let us look with joyful hope
Before whose brightness sin and death,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
